primary_citation: 5 U.S.C. §552a (Privacy Act of 1974, Pub. L. 93-579, 88 Stat. 1896, effective 1975-09-27)
short_title: Privacy Act — Federal Agency Records: Access, Amendment, and Civil Remedy
one_line_rule: Federal agencies must maintain accurate records and cannot disclose them without consent; individuals may access and amend their records, and sue for actual damages when agency failures cause adverse determinations or intentional privacy invasions.

case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: Plaintiff must prove actual damages for §552a(g)(1)(C) claim; adverse determination alone insufficient. §552a(g)(1)(D) $1,000 minimum floor does not require proving specific monetary harm when willfulness shown.

case_law.cite: Quinn v. Stone, No. 90-0412, 1991 WL 236996 (D.D.C. 1991); primary authority: Albright v. United States, 631 F.2d 915 (D.C. Cir. 1980)
case_law.court: U.S. District Court D.D.C. (applying D.C. Circuit Albright standard)
case_law.key_rule: 'Intentional or willful' = agency knew action was wrongful OR acted with reckless disregard for whether action was wrongful. Negligent mistake or clerical error insufficient.
